budget_items.what_was_said: The principal assessor reported abutters list requests and motor vehicle excise tax abatements processed in Munis this month, awaiting payment processing by the tax collector.
Four chapter land rollback tax invoices were sent to former chapter landowners in June; one has paid, one status unknown, two have not responded.

budget_items.topic: Functional/economic obsolescence discounts on chapter land, commercial and residential properties
budget_items.what_was_said: Inspections found undocumented obsolescence discounts on many properties dating back years, averaging around 60% with a range starting near 10%; the board asked for a spreadsheet to see the scope.

budget_items.topic: Chapter land (agricultural) use-value cost table update
budget_items.what_was_said: The principal assessor updated statewide chapter land cost/value figures, moving crop/vegetable/tobacco/soil/nursery land to an 'above average' rating; the board questioned whether reclassification was justified given the size of the increase.

budget_items.topic: FY2026 senior real estate exemption COLA
budget_items.what_was_said: The cost-of-living adjustment for the FY2026 senior real estate tax exemptions was confirmed and added to the updated exemption sheet.

Residential/commercial/industrial new growth for FY2026 was estimated, with personal property and utility appraisals still pending; last year's and this year's earlier estimates were recalled for comparison.

The principal assessor explained that seniors who did not qualify for the state circuit breaker cannot qualify for the new local senior means-tested exemption, and the circuit breaker can be claimed retroactively three years by the filer but not administratively by the assessors this first year.

budget_items.topic: 41 warrant article for income limitation increase
budget_items.what_was_said: The board needs to confirm the town meeting date so a warrant article raising the income limitation for exemptions can be prepared in time.

decisions.decision: Put the property obsolescence/abatement review (with correlation to prior abatements and recommendations) on the September 3rd agenda for a possible vote.
Until told otherwise, a person receiving a veteran exemption who also becomes eligible for the new senior means-tested exemption should be allowed to receive both.
Defer deciding the frequency/timing of senior-center outreach sessions to the September 3rd meeting.
Postpone DOR's request to limit land condition factors until neighborhood value corrections are further along; add to a future goals list.
Keep the updated 'above average' chapter land agricultural values as already entered for this year and research the history of the rating in the meantime.
If called for jury duty on the day of a future meeting, the board member will try to participate by phone rather than in person.
The principal assessor will draft a proposed response to the master-plan feedback questionnaire for the board to review before September 3rd.
Cancel the September 24th meeting (a member cannot attend) and set the next September date as TBD.

minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Board of Assessors received a lengthy status report from the principal assessor covering motor vehicle excise processing in the new Munis system, chapter land rollback taxes and applications, and a systematic finding of long-undocumented functional and economic obsolescence discounts on commercial and residential properties that the board is now reviewing property by property. The board also discussed FY2026 senior exemptions and the new circuit-breaker-linked senior means-tested exemption, updated statewide chapter land value tables, approved several sets of amended executive-session minutes, voted to decline purchasing a parcel on West Townsend Road, and set a plan to respond to a town master-plan feedback survey.

what_happened.line: Assessors found decades-old, undocumented valuation discounts on commercial, residential, and chapter land properties, and are reviewing them one by one.
The board set the property discount review for a possible vote at its September 3rd meeting.
The board voted to decline purchasing a parcel at 222 West Townsend Road.
The board discussed the new circuit-breaker-linked senior means-tested exemption and decided a senior can also keep a veteran exemption.

why_it_matters: A review of long-undocumented obsolescence discounts on commercial and residential properties could change what those owners are assessed once the board votes, which affects their tax bills.
A new senior means-tested exemption, tied to the state circuit-breaker credit, changes who qualifies for local property tax relief and how it can be combined with other exemptions.
Declining to purchase the West Townsend Road parcel keeps that land in private hands rather than town ownership.
